title: Operator Request Channel message (schema_version 1)
description: Common schema for OPREQ / OPRES / DEVREQ (requirement §6). Interpreted by roles/operator_request_channel/files/oprc/schema.py's validator, which supports exactly the keywords used in this document: type, properties, required, additionalProperties, enum, const, pattern, minLength, maxLength, minItems, maxItems, items. This document is the single source of truth for field-level constraints -- schema.py must never hardcode a second copy of any of them.

request_id.description: Server-assigned (requirement §6.1). A client submission must not set this key at all -- see oprc.schema.reject_server_assigned_fields, which runs before this field exists, not this pattern.

conversation_id.description: Set by the creator for a new OPREQ or standalone DEVREQ (its own conversation origin); inherited from the referenced message for a reply (requirement §6.2).

source.description: Server-assigned from the execution entry point (requirement §4.2), never trusted from the payload.

in_reply_to.description: Empty/null for a new OPREQ or a standalone DEVREQ; the referenced request_id for an OPRES or a reply DEVREQ (requirement §6.2).

created_at.description: Server-assigned: the receiving entry point's own clock, JST (requirement §6.1).

expires_at.description: Bounded by the deployment's max TTL; the receiving side rejects a value beyond that bound rather than clamping it silently.

repo_commit.description: The homelab-ansible commit the requester's working tree was at, if applicable. Optional: an Operator-authored OPRES/DEVREQ may have no single associated commit.

target_names.description: Inventory names or DNS names only -- IPv4-literal-shaped strings are rejected by pattern (requirement §6.3).

evidence_references.description: Opaque evidence pointers only (requirement §6.3) -- id is not a filesystem path and must not be treated as one downstream.
